Question: What is an allowance under PIA policy?
Answer: An allowance is a recurring or non-recurring payment other than pay granted to an employee.

Question: Who decides the rates of allowances?
Answer: Admissibility and rates of various allowances are determined by the PIACL Board of Directors, regulated under PIAC Employees (Service & Discipline) Regulations 1985.
Keywords: rates, board of directors, policy, regulation

Question: How much House Rent Allowance do I get?
Answer: Staff PG I-IV, Cabin Crew, Officers PG V-VIII, Officer Engineering, Aircraft Engineers and Deputy Chief Engineers get House Rent Allowance @ 45% of current basic pay per month.

Question: What about house rent for Pak-based employees posted abroad?
Answer: Pak-based employees permanently posted abroad get accommodation allowance at each station at rates approved from time to time by the Committee under Schedule of Powers.
Keywords: house rent, abroad, accommodation, foreign posting

Question: How much Conveyance/Car Maintenance Allowance do Officers get?
Answer: Admin Officers PG V-IX, Officer Engineering, Aircraft Engineers and Deputy Chief Engineers working in Pakistan get 10% of current basic pay per month, unless they are availing pickup/drop or a company car.

Question: How much Conveyance Allowance do staff get?
Answer: Staff PG I-II get Rs.900/month and PG III-IV get Rs.950/month.
Keywords: conveyance, staff, rate, PG I II III IV

Question: What if staff are provided pickup and drop by the Company?
Answer: Staff with route/road-side pickup and drop get 35% of the applicable conveyance allowance; the remaining 65% is adjusted/recovered. Staff with home pickup and drop get no conveyance allowance.

Question: When is Conveyance Allowance payable?
Answer: Only when the Company cannot provide transport. It's also payable during leave/temporary duty, and starts from the date company transport is stopped, provided the employee applies within a fortnight.

Question: Are contractual employees entitled to Conveyance Allowance?
Answer: Yes, if they are full-time employees already receiving pay on regular pay scales applicable to permanent employees.

Question: Is Conveyance Allowance paid during LPR?
Answer: Yes, it is admissible during LPR. Employees availing company pickup/drop get conveyance allowance of their pay scale during LPR.
Keywords: conveyance, LPR, leave prior to retirement

Question: How much Utility Allowance do I get?
Answer: Staff PG I-IV, Cabin Crew, Admin Officers PG V-IX, Officer Engineering and Aircraft Engineers get 10% of current basic pay per month.

Question: What is the Utility Allowance rate for Deputy Chief Engineers and above?
Answer: 10% of current basic pay per month, or the company entitlement prescribed for their equivalent cadre, whichever is higher.
Keywords: utility allowance, Deputy Chief Engineer, higher

Question: What is the Per Hour Flying Allowance for Cabin Crew?
Answer: It ranges by pay group from Rs.400/hour (PG IV & IV(i)) up to Rs.1300/hour (PG VIII, VIII(i), VII(ii)), calculated Blocks OFF to Blocks ON.
Keywords: cabin crew, flying allowance, per hour, pay group

Question: What is Non-Slip Allowance for cabin crew?
Answer: 30% of the total per-hour flying allowance, paid per hour from Blocks OFF to Blocks ON, only for up-and-down (base to base) flights.

Question: What is Domestic and International Layover Allowance for cabin crew?
Answer: Domestic Layover: Rs.100/hour from Blocks ON to Blocks OFF at slip stations. International Layover: US$4/hour, same basis (flight time excluded in both).
Keywords: layover allowance, domestic, international, cabin crew

Question: What is Grooming and Kit Allowance for cabin crew?
Answer: Rs.1000/month, paid to all female and male cabin crew.

Question: What is Assignment Allowance for cabin crew?
Answer: Flight Purser (PG VI): Rs.1500/month. Senior Purser (PG VII): Rs.2500/month. Training & Check Purser (PG VIII): Rs.3500/month. Not paid on transfer to ground duty or during leave exceeding 30 days at a stretch.

Question: What is LR (Long Range) Flight Allowance?
Answer: Rs.15,000 per person per flight for cabin crew operating Long Haul flights on Boeing 777 LR/ER on the PAK-CANADA-PAK sector.
Keywords: long range allowance, LR, 777, cabin crew

Question: What is Charter/Non-Charter Flight Allowance exceeding 16 hours?
Answer: Rs.15,000 per flight per person for cabin crew who consent to operate flights beyond the 16-hour Flight Duty Time Limitation.
Keywords: charter allowance, FDTL, 16 hours, cabin crew

Question: How is payment for Denied OFF Days calculated?
Answer: Cabin crew get 5 mandatory OFF days a month. Compensation for 2 denied OFF days is paid only to productive cabin crew, at 10 hours/day at the single flying allowance rate (i.e., 20 hours total), after verification by DGM Planning & Ops IT.
Keywords: denied off days, off days, cabin crew, compensation

Question: What is the DCCC (Designated Check Cabin Crew) Incentive?
Answer: Rs.5000 per flight check, plus Rs.5000 for practical training drills at PTC. 'G' code applies for DCCC with 100% flying allowance.

Question: What is Surface Travel Allowance for cabin crew?
Answer: Rs.500 per hour, for cabin crew travelling by surface from/to any base/station to operate or return from a flight, as per AIMS.

Question: What is Personal Pay for cabin crew?
Answer: Rs.150 per month, paid to Cabin Crew PG IV to VIII.

Question: What is the Flight Duty Time Limitation (FDTL) for cabin crew?
Answer: 16 hours including 2 hours of briefing and de-briefing time.
Keywords: FDTL, flight duty time, cabin crew

Question: What are the rest period rules for cabin crew?
Answer: At base: double the duty hours or 16 hours, whichever is more. Domestic outstation: 1.5x total duty or 10 hours, whichever is more. International outstation: 1.5x total duty or 12 hours, whichever is more (single-sector long-haul: 30 hours pre-flight rest, 45 hours at destination, 35 hours post-flight).

Question: What are the minimum flying hour requirements for domestic/regional/gulf flights?
Answer: Crew must operate a minimum of 50 hours on domestic/regional/gulf/non-slip flights over 2 consecutive months (25 hours/month planned). Failure means removal from international flights in the 3rd month plus a higher hour requirement (55 hours) that month.
Keywords: minimum flying hours, domestic, regional, gulf

Question: What are the standby duty rules for cabin crew?
Answer: At base: standby for 12 hours at residence. At outstations: standby for 24 hours after completing stipulated rest. Airport standby: 6 hours, duty commences on reporting at the briefing room. Duty beyond 16 hours from airport standby (up to 18 hours max) is treated as Access Duty for overtime.
Keywords: standby duty, cabin crew, access duty

Question: How does length of service affect a pilot's flying hour rate?
Answer: 0-10 years: +35% increase. 11-20 years: +30%. 21-30 years: +25%. 30+ years: +20%.
Keywords: flying hour rate, seniority, pilots, increase

Question: What are Guaranteed Flying Hours for pilots?
Answer: 50 guaranteed flying hours are paid to pilots if actual flying is minimum 40 hours, or if the month's assigned flying hours accumulate to less than 40 hours. Also applies during transition training (120 days) or recency training (30 days), and requires Privilege Leave of at least 7 consecutive days.

Question: When are pilots NOT entitled to the 50 guaranteed hours?
Answer: Unauthorized absence, insufficient privilege leave, refusal of assigned duty without valid reason, remedial training (actual hours paid instead), disciplinary suspension (paid if exonerated), habitual sick reports, or 3 consecutive months below guaranteed hours (where company average flying exceeds 40 hours).

Question: How is payment calculated for flying hours exceeding 50 guaranteed hours?
Answer: 51-60 hours: 150% of the flying hour rate. 61-70 hours: 200%. 71+ hours: 250%.

Question: What are the revised slip payment rates for pilots?
Answer: Domestic: Rs.750/hour (revised from Rs.250). International: US$10/hour (revised from US$5). This revision does not apply to pilots terminated, dismissed, or retired on or before 30 May 2023.
Keywords: slip payment, pilots, domestic, international, revised rate

Question: How is total pilot compensation structured?
Answer: Pilots get fixed pay comprising Basic Pay, House Rent, and a 50-hour Guaranteed Flying Allowance, plus 10 days off, all scaled by years of service (0-40 years) per the pay table in Admin Order 10/2023.
Keywords: pilot pay structure, basic pay, house rent, guaranteed flying allowance

Question: When is Flying Allowance paid to pilots?
Answer: From Blocks Off to Blocks On per the official flight log; the normal flying rate also applies to actual hours flown for Simulator PNF duties.
Keywords: flying allowance, blocks off blocks on, simulator

Question: What special rules apply to Executive and Instructor Pilots?
Answer: Special sick leave guaranteed hours capped at 30 weeks. No flying allowance increase for 2 years if a safety violation is proven. Instructor Pilots get 10 additional hours above guaranteed hours. Executive Pilots get 20 additional hours but are restricted to regional/domestic flying to maintain recency. Medical treatment for retired pilots' parents has been discontinued.
Keywords: executive pilots, instructor pilots, special rules

Question: What is Outstation Allowance for pilots?
Answer: Foreign stations: US$5/hour from blocks-on to blocks-off (flight time excluded), for international flights. Domestic stations: Rs.250/hour on the same basis.

Question: What happens if a pilot falls sick at an outstation?
Answer: Private doctor certificates are not accepted where company-designated doctors exist. Pilots get full medical attention from an approved doctor, or treatment expenditure is reimbursed if confirmed by the attending physician and flight surgeon.

Question: What allowance applies if a pilot falls sick while on duty abroad?
Answer: If hospitalized: 15% of Daily Allowance for the hospitalization period. If not hospitalized but sickness is certified by the Company Medical Officer: full Daily Allowance. The certificate must confirm the sickness disabled the crew member from travel.

Question: What allowance applies if a pilot falls sick on duty travel within Pakistan?
Answer: 15% of the applicable daily allowance rate if hospitalized. If not hospitalized, full daily allowance is admissible, subject to certification by GM (Medical Services), PIA Medical Officer, or the relevant Deputy Chief Medical Officer depending on the route.
Keywords: sickness within Pakistan, daily allowance, pilots

Question: What Daily Allowance applies during training/refresher duty abroad?
Answer: US$5.00 per hour from blocks-on to blocks-off at slip stations (flight time excluded), where no PIA establishment exists. Hotel accommodation and transportation are arranged by the Company.
Keywords: training abroad, daily allowance, refresher duty

Question: How are Refused Days Off paid for pilots?
Answer: Pilots get 7 days off at base each month. If utilized for flying duties with consent, they are entitled to payment at a uniform rate of 2 hours of Flying Allowance per refused day-off, certified by Chief Pilot Crew Planning & Scheduling.

Question: What happens if a pilot habitually misses assigned flights?
Answer: Payment of guaranteed hours is decided by the Chief of Flight Operations, and the pilot may be rostered for the missed flight pattern in subsequent months. No dead-heading credit is given, and no slip is allowed between the sick-report station and base.
Keywords: missed duty, sick reports, pilots, penalties

Question: What accommodation applies at unscheduled layover stations?
Answer: Government Rest House, Dak Bungalows, or Officers Mess (Defence) are acceptable where no First Class hotel exists. If a First Class hotel exists but has no availability, pilots are paid Rs.6000/day in lieu of hotel accommodation.

Question: What if a pilot needs medical treatment abroad?
Answer: If treatment isn't available locally, the pilot is sent abroad at Company expense on the Chief Flight Surgeon's recommendation, subject to competent authority approval, including hotel accommodation and travel facilities.

Question: What is Approval/Endorsement Allowance for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Narrow Body/Single Aisle B1/B2 AML: Rs.8000. Wide Body/Double Aisle B1/B2 AML: Rs.12,000. Overhaul Shop Class-I qualification: Rs.4000 each. Shop qualification equivalent to full B1/B2 set: Rs.8000. Capped at 4 aircraft full-set qualifications, ceiling Rs.28,000.
Keywords: approval allowance, endorsement, aircraft engineers, AML

Question: What conditions apply to Endorsement Allowance?
Answer: It applies only to aircraft types existing in the PIA fleet, and the engineer must perform duty on that aircraft (directly, indirectly, or per company requirement). Two OFFs may be paid to both B1 and B2 engineers against each type qualification.

Question: What is Special Allowance for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Ranges by AEPS grade A-G from Rs.24,918 to Rs.51,485/month (w.e.f. 01-08-2016). Deputy Chief Engineers (grades D-G): Rs.44,159-57,485. Chief Engineers (grades D-G): Rs.52,866-65,477. Chief Technical Officer (grades D-G): Rs.54,866-67,477.
Keywords: special allowance, aircraft engineers, AEPS grade

Question: What is Special Pay for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Ranges by AEPS grade A-G from Rs.52,212 to Rs.100,242/month. Deputy Chief Engineers: Rs.88,125-118,402. Chief Engineers: Rs.95,265-123,042. Chief Technical Officer (F-G): Rs.119,385-127,042. Special Allowance and Special Pay were restored from 50% to 100% w.e.f. 1 November 2022.

Question: What is Executive Allowance for Deputy Chief/Chief Engineers?
Answer: Deputy Chief Engineers (D-G): Rs.12,808-15,363/month. Chief Engineers (D-G): Rs.27,706-28,618/month. Chief Technical Officer: same as other Departmental Heads.

Question: What is Airworthiness Approval Allowance?
Answer: Paid by AEPS grade (Rs.36,221 to Rs.76,366/month) for qualifications on which the engineer was initially placed in AEPS, and continues even if that aircraft type leaves the PIA fleet.

Question: What is Airworthiness Certification Allowance and how is it calculated?
Answer: Per landing: Domestic Rs.1500, International up to 6 hours Rs.3000, 6-8 hours Rs.4000, 8+ hours Rs.5000. Paid per Flight Number (domestic/international). If diverted without landing, engineers are compensated Rs.1500 flat. Test flights get Rs.4000 fixed plus life insurance coverage.
Keywords: airworthiness certification allowance, per landing, aircraft engineers

Question: What accommodation/meal benefits apply to Aircraft Engineers on flying duty?
Answer: Transportation and hotel accommodation match cockpit crew entitlement. If no First-Class hotel is available domestically and the engineer arranges his own stay, Rs.7000/night domestic is paid in addition to normal G.D/OCS allowance. Meals are provided at par with cockpit crew.
Keywords: accommodation, meals, aircraft engineers, flying duty

Question: What is Shift/Night Allowance for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Shift Allowance: 6% of Basic Pay/month for rotating shifts. Night Allowance: Rs.900/night for duty performed between 2330 and 0630 hours.
Keywords: shift allowance, night allowance, aircraft engineers

Question: What is Extended Duty/Denied Rest Allowance for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: 1% of current basic pay per hour, payable in Pakistan only, with prior Chief Engineer approval. No day-off is given in lieu. Capped at 24 hours/person/month and a budget of Rs.15 million/year. Paid via voucher/cheque by the 20th of every month.
Keywords: extended duty, denied rest, aircraft engineers

Question: What is General Declaration (G.D.) Travel Expense for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Domestic stations: Rs.150/hour (Blocks ON to Blocks OFF, flight time excluded). International stations: US$5.00/hour on the same basis. For VVIP flights, the rate is doubled and the full expected hours are paid in advance.
Keywords: GD travel expense, general declaration, aircraft engineers

Question: What are the duty time limits for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Ground duty limit is 8 hours, extendable to 16 hours in emergencies, but not more than 48 hours extended duty/denied rest in a month. Engineers should not be regularly scheduled beyond 8 hours.
Keywords: duty time limitation, aircraft engineers, 8 hours

Question: What is Split Duty Allowance for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Rs.6000/month with Chief's approval, in addition to shift allowance if applicable. Transport is provided for the second duty in a day.

Question: What is Hardship Allowance for Aircraft Engineers?
Answer: Rs.3000/month for duties performed at stations designated as hardship stations by the Company.

Question: What allowances make up the base package for Officer Engineering?
Answer: Personal Pay: 5% of current basic pay. House Rent/Accommodation: 45% of current basic pay. Conveyance/Car Maintenance Allowance: 10% of current basic pay - all per month.
Keywords: officer engineering, personal pay, house rent, conveyance

Question: What is Special Allowance for Officer Engineering?
Answer: By OEPS grade: A=Rs.1000, B=Rs.1300, C=Rs.2500, D=Rs.6000, E=Rs.8500 per month.
Keywords: special allowance, officer engineering, OEPS grade

Question: What is Class-II/Class-III Approval Allowance for Officers Engineering?
Answer: Class-III: Rs.500/month per approval. Class-II: Rs.1400/month per approval for Narrow Body, Rs.1600 for Wide Body. Maximum combined ceiling: Rs.12,200/month.
Keywords: class II class III approval, officer engineering

Question: What is Shift/Night Allowance for Officer Engineering?
Answer: Shift Allowance: 6% of basic pay. Officers detailed on Night Shift duties also get an additional Rs.350/night for actual night duty performed (2330-0630 hours, excluding flying duty).
Keywords: shift allowance, night allowance, officer engineering

Question: What are the smaller fixed allowances for Officer Engineering?
Answer: Overhaul/Maintenance Allowance: Rs.1000/month. Towing Allowance: Rs.1000/month (not paid beyond 90 days' leave). Welding Allowance: Rs.700/month. Crew Chief Allowance: Rs.1000/month for designated Crew Chiefs. Hill Hardship Allowance: Rs.2000/month.
Keywords: overhaul allowance, towing allowance, welding allowance, crew chief, hill hardship, officer engineering

Question: What is Outstation Allowance for Officer Engineering on flying duties?
Answer: Domestic: Rs.60/hour or Rs.1000/hour of flying duty, whichever is more. International: US$3/hour plus Rs.1500/landing.
Keywords: outstation allowance, officer engineering, flying duties

Question: What is GD Travel Expense for Officer Engineering (non-slip flights)?
Answer: Domestic flights: Rs.1000. International flights up to 6 hours: Rs.1500. Up to 8 hours: Rs.2000.
Keywords: GD travel expense, officer engineering, non-slip

Question: What is Extended Duty/Denied Rest payment for Officer Engineering?
Answer: 1% of current basic pay per hour, payable in Pakistan only, capped at 24 hours/person/month and a Rs.12.5 million budget. Excess hours beyond the cap convert to day-off (8 hours extended duty = 1 day off).
Keywords: extended duty, denied rest, officer engineering

Question: What is Grooming Allowance for Officers Engineering?
Answer: Rs.2000/month, paid only to female Officers Engineering.

Question: What allowances do DGMs, GMs and Chiefs (Admin Category) get?

Chiefs: House Rent 121,000, Utility 34,848, Assignment Pay 87,120, Fuel 432 litres, Car Maintenance 12,672, Driver's Pay 19,008 - all PKR per month.
Keywords: DGM, GM, chiefs, house rent, assignment pay, fuel, driver pay

Question: Is there a Special Allowance for Chiefs in Admin Category?
Answer: Yes, Rs.9000 per month.

Question: What is Personal Pay and Special Allowance for Officers PG V-IX?
Answer: Personal Pay: 5% of Basic Pay (except Cabin Crew). Special Allowance by PG: V=Rs.2500, VI=Rs.3500, VII=Rs.4500, VIII=Rs.7000, IX=Rs.8500 per month.
Keywords: personal pay, special allowance, officers PG V IX

Question: What is Non-Practicing Allowance for Medical Officers?
Answer: Rs.25,000/month for permanent Medical Officers/Doctors. Medical Officers PG-VIII and above with 20 years' service can do private practice only if they surrender this allowance. Others cannot engage in private practice at all.

Question: What is Trim Sheet Allowance for Officers PG-V?
Answer: Rs.250 per licence per aircraft, subject to a maximum of Rs.2500/month for qualified Officers in PG-V holding a Trim Sheet Licence.
Keywords: trim sheet allowance, officers PG V

Question: What is Towing Allowance for Officers in Technical Ground Support?
Answer: Rs.600/month for Officers in PG-V, V(i), V(ii) with valid CAA Towing Licence, assigned towing duty. Not paid during approved leave beyond 90 days.
Keywords: towing allowance, technical ground support, officers

Question: How are Pak-based officers at foreign stations paid?
Answer: Basic Pay, Personal Pay, and Qualification Allowance are paid in local currency.

Question: What is Personal Pay for Staff PG I-IV?
Answer: 5% of current basic pay per month, for all employees in staff cadre except cabin crew.
Keywords: personal pay, staff PG I IV

Question: What are the small fixed monthly allowances for staff (Messengers, Attendants, etc.)?
Answer: Messengers (Communication Division): Rs.250. Uniform Compensation (no uniform entitlement): Rs.800. Office Attendants (Central Registry): Rs.250. Office Attendants (general): Rs.400. Towing Allowance: Rs.225. Machine Allowance: Rs.175. Unit Leader Allowance: Rs.150 - all per month.
Keywords: messengers, office attendants, towing, machine, unit leader, staff allowances

Question: What is Approval Allowance for Technicians in Engineering?
Answer: Class-III: Rs.500/approval/month. Class-II: Rs.1200/approval for Narrow Body, Rs.1500 for Wide Body. Maximum ceiling: Rs.7500/month.

Question: What is Trim Sheet Allowance for staff?
Answer: Rs.300 per licence per aircraft, subject to a maximum ceiling of Rs.3000/month.

Question: What is Overhaul Allowance for staff?
Answer: Rs.250/month, for staff working in specific shop codes (E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8, E9, EA, EB, EC, ED, EE, EL, EM, ER, ES, ET, EU, EV, EW).

Question: What is Baggage/Cargo Handling Allowance?
Answer: Rs.255/month, for all Baggage/Cargo Attendants in Pay Group I to IV(ii).

Question: What is Cash Handling Allowance?
Answer: Rs.500/month for Accounts Staff dealing with cash functions, and also payable to Reservation & Ticketing Staff assigned cash handling duties at domestic service/reservation counters.
Keywords: cash handling allowance, accounts staff, reservation staff

Question: What is Flight Equipment Allowance and Kit Maintenance Allowance?
Answer: Flight Equipment Allowance: Rs.275/month for Technical Staff in Engineering & Maintenance and Flight Simulator section. Kit Maintenance Allowance: Rs.275/month for staff entitled to uniform.
Keywords: flight equipment allowance, kit maintenance allowance, staff

Question: What is Bhatta Allowance?
Answer: Rs.25 per duty, admissible to Motor Transport Drivers.

Question: What is Deputy/Head Loader Allowance?
Answer: Rs.225/month.

Question: What is Technical Pay for staff?
Answer: PG I/II: Rs.325/month. PG III/IV: Rs.350/month.
Keywords: technical pay, staff, PG I II III IV

Question: What is Welding Allowance for staff?
Answer: PG I: Rs.150/month. PG II: Rs.275/month. PG III/IV: Rs.550/month.

Question: What is Electrical Wireman/Supervisor Licence Allowance?
Answer: For Staff PG III-IV in Works Division: Electrical Wireman Rs.350/month, Electrical Supervisor Rs.450/month.
Keywords: electrical wireman, electrical supervisor, licence allowance

Question: What is Navigation Baggage Allowance?
Answer: Rs.200/month.

Question: What is Computer Allowance for IT staff?
Answer: Computer Operator/Assistant Programmer (PG IV): Rs.1300/month. Trainee Programmer (PG III): Rs.1000/month. Data Entry Operator/DEPAK Operator (PG III): Rs.600/month - for staff working on Mainframe Computer in the IT Department.

Question: What is Aircraft Sanitation Allowance?
Answer: Rs.250/month, for Aircraft Cleaners in Engineering Department working on aircraft.

Question: What is Leave Travel Allowance (LTA)?
Answer: 15 days of current Basic Pay, as per applicable Company rules.

Question: What is Technical Allowance for Ramp Services technicians?
Answer: Rs.300/month for Maintenance & Technical Staff PG III/IV (Admin) working in Ramp Services at Karachi and domestic stations.

Question: What is the allowance for dual-function Pantry-man-cum-Operator?
Answer: Rs.350-625/month for staff in Food Service Division (Pakistan only) designated as Catering Operators performing dual functions; paid separately and counted for overtime purposes.
Keywords: pantry man, catering operator, dual function

Question: What is Special Remuneration Allowance?
Answer: Up to Rs.1500/month, admissible to employees PG I-V for performing any additional duty or duty of an arduous nature.

Question: What is Special Duty Travel Allowance for Security Personnel?
Answer: Security Officer: Rs.40/hour. Security Supervisor/Assistant: Rs.30/hour - for escort duty involving foreign travel on the same flight, paid from departure to arrival in Pakistan. Not paid together with Daily Allowance (whichever is more applies in delays); paid in lieu of discontinued Flying Allowance.
Keywords: special duty travel allowance, security personnel

Question: What is Meal Allowance?
Answer: Rs.100 per duty, admissible where canteen facility is not available, paid via ERP Self Service Request.

Question: What is the general Grooming Allowance?
Answer: Rs.1000/month, paid to all female Staff and Officers.
Keywords: grooming allowance, female staff, officers, general

Question: What is Firewood Allowance?
Answer: Staff PG I-IV: Rs.4000/month. Officers PG V and above: Rs.4500/month. Payable for 6 months a year (1 October to 31 March) at stations like Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Delbadin, Kharan, Khuzdar, Loralai, Ormara, Panjgur, Quetta, Taftan, Zhob, Abbottabad, Chitral, Gilgit, Saidu Sharif, and Skardu.

Question: What is Hill/Hardship Allowance and which areas qualify?
Answer: Staff PG I-IV: Rs.1500/month. Officers PG V/VI: Rs.1560/month. Officers PG VII+: Rs.1560/month. Hilly areas include Mirpur, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot (AJK); Delbadin, Gwadar, Jiwani, Kharan, Khuzdar, Loralai, Ormara, Panjgur, Pasni, Quetta, Sibbi, Sui, Taftan, Turbat, Zhob (Balochistan); Abbottabad, Baltistan, Chilas, Chitral, Gilgit Agency, Saidu Sharif, Skardu, Swabi, Tarbela (KPK/FATA); and Murree (Punjab).
Keywords: hill hardship allowance, hilly areas, stations

Question: What is Special Pay Gilgit/Skardu?
Answer: 25% of Basic Pay per month, which ceases on transfer out of Northern Areas and does not count toward PF, gratuity, pension, or bonus.

Question: What Flying Allowance applies to non-cabin-crew officers/staff?
Answer: Security Assistants/Supervisors on PIA flights: Rs.16/flying hour. Flight Ops operational staff: Rs.16/hour; operational officers: Rs.35/hour. Customer Services Traffic Officers (VIP/VVIP coverage): Rs.35/hour. Operational Engineers: Rs.45/flying hour (blocks off to blocks on).
Keywords: flying allowance, non cabin crew, operational staff

Question: What is the Daily Allowance policy for OCS/temporary duty?
Answer: Travelling & Daily Allowance is paid to Officers and Staff (other than Pilots) required to travel on OCS/temporary duty within Pakistan or to foreign stations, per rates in Appendix E.

Question: What happens if temporary duty abroad exceeds 30 days?
Answer: Daily Allowance rates gradually decrease per Appendix E for durations of temporary duty, training, or refresher beyond 30 days.

Question: What is the Daily Allowance rule for permanent posting abroad?
Answer: TA/DA is paid for a maximum of 30 days. If TA/DA is taken in lieu of accommodation, the employee does not get group-wise accommodation allowance during that period.

Question: What approval is needed for OCS travel abroad?
Answer: Prior approval must be obtained from the CEO, routed through the concerned Chief and CHRO in all cases, clearly indicating the purpose and days of TA/DA involved.

Question: Who is eligible for Education Allowance when posted abroad?
Answer: Pak-based employees posted abroad for a normal 3-year period, covering up to 3 children with Pakistani nationality, studying Class I-X or equivalent (O-level British or up to Grade XII American), aged 6 to 18 years.

Question: What schools are covered under Education Allowance?
Answer: Pak Embassy Schools, institutions managed by other Muslim countries, or comparable community/missionary schools - not American or British schools as a matter of policy, and only at stations where the medium of instruction is not English.

Question: How much does the Company pay for tuition under Education Allowance?
Answer: Up to US$275 per month per child, for tuition fee only, reimbursed against submission of the proper school fee receipt.

Question: What is the alternative to claiming tuition fee reimbursement?
Answer: Employees who don't claim tuition fee can get Rs.1500/month/child (up to 3 children) in lieu, with a submitted undertaking verified by the Area/Station Head, no receipt required.

Question: In which countries is Education Allowance applicable?
Answer: Applicable in Europe (Belgium, Austria, CIS Stations, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Netherlands, Switzerland, Turkey), Far East (Australia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Nepal, Philippines, South Korea, Thailand), and Middle East/Africa (Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Johannesburg, Kenya, Kuwait, Somalia, Syria, Tanzania, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Iran, Iraq, Libya, Oman, North Yemen, Qatar, UAE).

Question: Where is Education Allowance NOT applicable?
Answer: Canada, Russia, United Kingdom, USA (Europe/America); and China, Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Myanmar, Singapore (Far East).

Question: What happens if a posting abroad is extended beyond the normal period?
Answer: Education Allowance continues if the posting is extended on Company requirement, payable monthly with competent authority approval, for the remaining posting period, provided the country is on the applicable list.

Question: What is Entertainment Allowance (Accountable)?
Answer: A position-related allowance for Area/Station Heads, Sectional Heads, and field staff doing sales promotion, to entertain clients, agents, government officials and allied organizations. It is accountable and not part of take-home salary.

Question: How is Entertainment Allowance reimbursed?
Answer: Subject to submission of bills, vouchers, and a statement of expenditure incurred the preceding month; Finance/Accounts Managers cannot reimburse without bills/vouchers within the approved ceiling.

Question: What is Entertainment Expenses (Accountable) for office use?
Answer: Allocated to Executive officers for day-to-day office expenses (newspapers, magazines, tea/refreshment). Rates: GMs & equivalent up to PKR 4650, Chiefs & equivalent up to PKR 7700, CEO up to PKR 11,350.
Keywords: entertainment expenses, office, GM, chiefs, CEO

Question: What is the Kilometre Allowance rate within Pakistan?
Answer: Rs.15 per kilometre, for Officers & Staff using own/hired transport for official duties beyond normal assignment, and for Sales Promotion Officials, subject to a monthly ceiling per station.

Question: What approval is needed for Kilometre Allowance?
Answer: Prior approval of the Area/Station Head (domestic stations) or concerned GM and above (Head Office), with a transport requisition signed by the local MT Incharge confirming whether a PIA vehicle was provided.

Question: What is Mileage Allowance during OCS travel?
Answer: Rs.7/km for officers travelling by road (own private car) where stations are not connected by air, subject to certification of exact distance. Train/public transport is reimbursed at actual fare with original receipts.

Question: Is there a distance ceiling for Kilometre Allowance?
Answer: Yes, payment cannot exceed the station-wise ceiling specified in Appendix H (e.g., Karachi/Lahore 1100 km/month, Islamabad/Rawalpindi 1000 km/month, Peshawar 900 km/month, Quetta 600 km/month); for unlisted stations, actual distance covered applies.

Question: Who is eligible for Transport Allowance (Mileage Expense) as Sales Promotion Officers?
Answer: District Manager, District Sales Manager, Pax/Cargo Sales Manager, Assistant District/Pax/Cargo Sales Manager, Sr. Sales Promotion Officer, Sales Promotion Officer, Sales Representative (Pax/Cargo), DGM Pax/Cargo Sales (Corporate), and Manager Interline/Interline Officers.
Keywords: transport allowance, sales promotion officers, eligibility

Question: What are the Mileage Expense rates for Sales Promotion Officers?
Answer: Own car: Rs.7/km. Company car/transport used for official duty: Rs.5/km. No personal conveyance: Rs.7/km - all subject to the monthly ceiling allocated at the station.
Keywords: mileage expense, rates, sales promotion officers

Question: Can Sales Promotion Officers get both Mileage Expense and Conveyance Allowance?
Answer: Yes, officers paid Mileage Expense are also entitled to Car Maintenance/Conveyance Allowance in addition, as admissible under the rules.

Question: What is the Kilometre reimbursement rate for Pak-based staff at foreign stations?
Answer: UK: US$2/mile. Toronto: US$3/km. Doha: US$0.32/km. UAE: US$0.48/km. Saudi Arabia: US$0.52/km. China: US$0.75/km. Kuwait: US$1/km. Baku: US$1.25/km - for inter-city/within-city travel where company conveyance isn't available.
Keywords: kilometre reimbursement, foreign stations, sales promotion

Question: What are the general rules for approving overtime?
Answer: No non-operational staff is detailed on overtime (day-off instead); OT is only allowed in shift-based operational areas; no OT is allowed if unplanned absenteeism is up to 10%; Karachi/Islamabad GM and above only approve OT.

Question: When does overtime get paid at double rate on holidays?
Answer: For PG IV and below (except Cabin Crew), double rate applies on 5 Company holidays: 1st day of Eid-ul-Fitr, 10th of Zilhaj, 10th of Moharram, Eid-e-Milad un Nabi or Dasehra (for Hindu employees), and Quaid-e-Azam's Birthday and Christmas.

Question: Is overtime paid for investigation-related detention?
Answer: Yes, employees PG I-IV detained beyond normal hours for disciplinary case investigation are paid overtime for the actual hours detailed by the Investigation Officer, but not during suspension.

Question: What rest periods apply for shift workers doing overtime?
Answer: Workers required to work 12-16 hours at a stretch get a minimum 12-hour rest; those working beyond 16 hours get a minimum 24-hour rest. Rest falling in the next duty period counts as idle time for wage calculation.

Question: How is overtime calculated for PG I-IV employees?
Answer: Using the formula: basic pay plus all allowances, divided by 208, on a weekly basis (week = days 1-7, 8-14, 15-21, 22-28). Working hours under 48/week are paid single rate; hours exceeding 48/week are paid double rate.
Keywords: overtime calculation, formula, PG I IV

Question: Is overtime paid through separate vouchers?
Answer: No, overtime is only paid along with the monthly salary. Contractual/daily-wage employees are also entitled to overtime, even if not stated in their contract.
Keywords: overtime payment, monthly salary, contractual employees

Question: How is double overtime calculated for holiday shifts spanning midnight?
Answer: Shifts that fall entirely or partly within a holiday's 0000-0000 window get double overtime for the hours that fall within the holiday period.

Question: How much is Settling-In Allowance on permanent transfer?
Answer: Married or Widow/Widower with children: 2 months' Basic Pay. Unmarried or Widow/Widower with no children: 1 month's Basic Pay.

Question: When is Settling-In Allowance NOT paid?
Answer: For self-requested transfers, for new entrants posted at a station other than their recruitment station (not treated as 'transfer'), and if a permanent re-transfer happens within 3 months of the last transfer.

Question: What if free accommodation is provided by the Company?
Answer: Only 50% of the applicable Settling-In Allowance is paid.

Question: What if both husband and wife are PIA employees transferred to the same station?
Answer: Only one gets full transfer benefits; the other gets 50% of Settling-In Allowance only (no packing/loading/transport charges for luggage), though both retain personal car transport benefits if the car is individually registered.
Keywords: settling-in allowance, husband wife, both PIA employees

Question: What are the Shift Allowance rates by pay group?
Answer: PG I/II: Rs.375/month. PG III/IV: Rs.410/month. PG V: Rs.500/month. PG VI: Rs.600/month. PG VII and above: Rs.700/month.

Question: How is Shift Allowance affected by leave?
Answer: Leave under 15 days in a calendar month with resumption of shift work: full rate. Leave 15-20 days: 50% of applicable rate. Leave over 20 days: no shift allowance.

Question: What are Night Shift Allowance rates?
Answer: PG I-II: Rs.84/night. PG III-IV: Rs.102/night. PG V, VI, VII and above: Rs.250/night - for actual night duty performed between 2330 and 0630 hours; not paid in addition to overtime where applicable.

Question: What special allowance applies to staff in the Chairman/CEO's Secretariat?
Answer: In lieu of overtime, meal allowance & taxi charges: Special Assistants Rs.10,000, Dy GM PG-IX Rs.8,600, Managers/Asst Managers PG VII/VIII Rs.7,200, Officers PG V/VI Rs.6,000, Staff PG III/IV Rs.4,800, Staff PG I/II Rs.3,600, Secretary to Chairman/CEO Rs.3,000, Protocol Officers PG V/VI Rs.7,200, Drivers Rs.3,000, Security Guard PG I/II Rs.4,000 per month. Ceases on posting out of the Secretariat.

Question: What special allowance applies to staff in the Corporate Secretariat?
Answer: Officer: Rs.10,000/month. Staff: Rs.5,000/month. Ceases on posting out of the Corporate Secretariat.

Question: What is the Special Allowance for Flight Operations Officer License Holders?
Answer: Rs.2000/month, subject to holding a valid PCAA license, being properly utilized in Flight Dispatch/Central Control at domestic stations, and not being on leave 30+ days.

Question: What is the CRM Training Allowance?

Question: Who qualifies for Qualification Allowance for Professional Accountants?
Answer: Associate & Fellow members of ICAP, ICMAP, ACCA-UK, CIMA-UK, or CFA-USA, restricted to staff working in Finance Department and Internal Audit Division only.

Question: What are the Qualification Allowance rates for accountants?
Answer: By Pay Group (ICAP/ICMA rate / ACCA-CIMA-CFA rate): Chief Rs.190,000/150,000; PG-X Rs.140,000/110,000; PG-IX Rs.90,000/70,000; PG-VIII Rs.65,000/50,000; PG-VII Rs.50,000/40,000; PG-VI/V Rs.30,000/25,000 per month.

Question: What if an officer holds two or more qualifications?
Answer: Only the highest single qualification amount is paid, not a combination.

Question: Who is eligible for IT Proficiency Pay?
Answer: Officers PG-V and above working in the Information Communication Technology Department, holding relevant Master's/Bachelor's degrees (Computer Science, IT, Engineering related fields) or with 15+ years' service in specific IT roles.

Question: What are the IT Proficiency Pay rates?
Answer: Category A: Rs.10,000/month. Category B: Rs.30,000/month. Category C: Rs.40,000/month - only one category is paid regardless of how many certifications the officer holds.

Question: When is IT Proficiency Pay discontinued?
Answer: For suspended employees, those under Show Cause Notice, those with two warning letters in the same financial year, and during LPR (except encashment). Resumption needs fresh Director/Chief approval.

Question: Can Computer Allowance and IT Proficiency Pay be drawn together?
Answer: No, Computer Allowance is not paid to those drawing IT Proficiency Pay.
Keywords: IT proficiency pay, computer allowance, combined

Question: What allowances are payable to Pak-based employees at foreign stations?

Question: What are the Maternity Allowance rates?
Answer: Normal delivery: Rs.20,000. Minor surgical intervention: Rs.25,000. Caesarean case: Rs.35,000.

Question: How do PG I-IV married employees claim Maternity Allowance?
Answer: Via an application certified by the Sectional Head, supported by a birth certificate from local authorities, submitted within 90 days of the certificate's issuance. Only permanent PG I-IV employees, or contractual employees with a minimum 2-year contract on equivalent pay scales, are eligible.
Keywords: maternity allowance, PG I IV, claim procedure

Question: How do Officers PG-V and above claim Maternity Allowance?
Answer: By submitting a claim for reimbursement of maternity charges to the Chief Medical Officer/Chief Flight Surgeon through their HR/Business Manager, who verifies the claim.
Keywords: maternity allowance, PG V and above, claim procedure

Question: What documents are required for a Maternity Allowance claim?
Answer: Original hospital/maternity home bill and cash receipt; medical store receipts with prescriptions; photocopy of birth certificate; blood group (if any); laboratory receipts (if any); and discharge certificate/card.
